status: Existing memory semantics approved for the proposed paired acquired-life control; actual harness review pending.
candidate: On a private Brain.load of each original checkpoint, attach SynapticMemory(brain.sensory_index, brain.motor_index, consolidation=0.05); control retains hippocampus=None. No other configuration, state or history changes.
findings: Exactly matches existing Brain constructor episodic=True pathway. New matrix is empty and writes=0; this restores a supported component, not a new learning mechanism.

Brain._record keys the original observation and writes actual delivered scalar reward at each executed motor slot index. value_mask excludes all unchosen alternatives. A row is counted once, although all chosen slot components receive the shared outcome.

Active sampled outcomes record through Brain.learn; the outcome waking a routine brain is recorded once through Brain.live. Accepted-feedback/answer-refusal retry does not restore the pending outcome; bootstrap refusal restores memory arrays and separator state.
FastSynapses.recall is read-only; SynapticMemory decays residuals only during observation. Retrieval supplies motor drive before full graph qualification, not an external answer or override.

Brain.reset retains fast and consolidated associative memory, although it resets live trace/arousal/pending action. A continuing acquired-life arm should not reset. A private frozen evaluation may use its prescribed reset, but must not call hippocampus.reset unless explicitly testing loss of fast memory.
FrozenPolicy.act(greedy=True) reads memory and evolves private working trace without new reward writes. predict/accuracy bypass memory and are unsuitable substitutes for this retrieval control.

Attaching empty memory before the real pending outcome preserves that outcome and may record it as the first actual write. Do not replay earlier rewards or manufacture past records; do not recompute the prior saved record forecast.

Memory remains a finite cue-to-per-slot outcome association. It does not identify individual motor causal contributions or store a joint-action value table, and correlated cues may interfere. Behavioral success must still be measured.
